newsitem.title: USA: CME feeders end mixed, live cattle mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME feeders end mixed, live cattle mostly lower.

text.p: Late profit taking weighed on CME feeder cattle futures after values again posted new contract highs and prices ended mixed, traders said. Live cattle ended mostly lower in light trade.
Feeder cattle closed up 0.250 cent per lb to off 0.250 with August off 0.100 at 76.550 cents after posting a new high of 76.975 early. All but January and March posted new highs.
Live cattle ended up 0.050 cent a lb to off 0.250 with June off 0.050 at 65.400 cents. October set a new high of 69.125 cents, then fell.
Feeder cattle set new contract highs for the sixth time in the past seven trading sessions before retreating.

Late profit taking encountered little follow-through demand in feeders as most months of live cattle and both pork pits ended lower. Early strength came from an overall strong tone to cash feeders and May ended up despite a decline in the latest CME feeder cattle index, traders said.
The latest CME feeder index fell $0.19 to $72.13 per cwt.
"May is up because they are looking for an increase in the index on lower (cattle) numbers in the direct markets last week," said Dan Vaught, analyst for AG Edwards.
Recent active feedlot cattle sales should reinforce interest for feeders, especially if feed costs remain relatively low, compared with last year, traders added.
Refco sold late after buying early along with Prudential Securities and local short covering which lifted prices up into buy stops, pit sources said.

Nearby live cattle futures drifted on both sides of previous levels much of the day with late spreading of long August/short June making for a mixed close in those months. Deferred contracts slipped for losses on scattered selling after a new high was posted in October, traders said.

Nearbys exhibited little direction as packer-related comercial hedge lifting met feedlot-related hedge selling. Current strength in wholesale beef prices as well as feedlot cattle sparked buying but seasonal considerations kept a lid on the market, they said.

Fed cattle supplies are projected to increase soon, based on recent USDA Cattle-on-Feed reports and beef prices are seen topping soon after retailers finish purchases of beef to meet upcoming late spring and early summer holidays.
Early indications on the next Cattle-on-Feed report are starting to weigh on back months, traders said.
"There is some bearishness coming in here on what the Cattle-on-Feed report is going to say with almost everybody looking for high numbers compared to last year," Vaught said.
Vaught added that on-feed supplies at the start of March were likely a record since the 1992 start of the current reporting system.
Refco and Cargill lightly spread long August/short June in the live cattle pit, sources said.
In live cattle options, commercials were doing the 66/76 put spread while commission houses sold June 66 calls. Volitility was steady, pit sources added.
